category.title: Legs
category.intro: Programmes that strengthen the front and back of the thighs and the glutes. You start with sitting down onto a chair and standing up, and progress through lunges, Bulgarian split squats and jump squats.
science: Sets with light loads done close to failure can build as much muscle as heavy loads (an analysis of 21 studies); for maximum strength, heavy loads work better.
Without equipment, the best way to add load is single-leg moves; the Bulgarian split squat works the glutes more than a normal squat.
Static holds such as the wall sit were among the exercises that lowered blood pressure most in an analysis combining 270 studies.
Keep your knees pointing the same way as your toes; if your knee hurts, reduce the depth of the move.

exercises.name: Chair Squat
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes (easy)
exercises.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy chair with your back to it. Feet shoulder-width apart.
steps: Push your hips back and sit down slowly onto the chair; reach your arms forward.
Stop when your hips lightly touch the chair.
Push through your heels to stand up.
exercises.tip: The safest way to learn the squat; over time, just touch the chair without sitting.
exercises.mistake: Don't drop onto the chair; sit with control.

exercises.name: Squat
exercises.target: Front of the thighs, glutes and hamstrings
exercises.setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
steps: Push your hips back and lower down; reach your arms forward.
Stop when your thighs are close to parallel with the floor; chest up.
Push through your heels to stand up.
exercises.tip: Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your knees cave in or your heels lift off the floor.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.setup: Lean your back against a wall and place your feet two steps in front of it.
steps: Slide your back down the wall until your knees are at 90 degrees.
Keep your knees above your heels.
Keep breathing and hold until the time is up.
exercises.tip: If it's too hard, hold higher, with your knees open wider than 90 degrees.
exercises.mistake: Don't press on your knees with your hands; don't hold your breath.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes
steps: Take a big step back with one foot and lower by bending both knees.
Stop when your back knee nears the floor; your front knee is over your ankle.
Push through your front heel to return to the start; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: The reverse lunge is kinder to the knee than the forward lunge.
exercises.mistake: Don't lean your body forward; stay upright.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes
exercises.setup: One foot forward, the other a step behind, back heel lifted.
steps: Without moving your feet, bend both knees and lower straight down.
Stop when your back knee nears the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand up; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: If your balance is shaky, support yourself with one hand on a wall.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your front knee cave in.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes (hard)
exercises.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy chair; put the top of one foot on the chair behind you. Your front foot is a step ahead.
steps: Bend your front knee and lower straight down.
Stop when your back knee nears the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand up; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: The further forward your front foot is, the more your glutes work.
exercises.mistake: Don't push with your back leg; let the front leg do the work.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes
exercises.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy step or a low chair; put one foot on top.
steps: Press through the top heel to step up onto it.
Stand tall at the top.
Step back down slowly with the same leg; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: The higher the step, the harder it gets; don't let your knee go above hip height.
exercises.mistake: Don't jump up off the foot on the floor.

exercises.name: Side Lunge
exercises.target: Front of the thighs, inner thighs and glutes
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet wide, toes pointing forward. Bring your hands together at your chest.
steps: Shift your weight onto one leg and sit to the side by bending that knee; keep the other leg straight.
Hips back, chest up.
Push back to the middle; switch sides halfway through.
exercises.tip: You should feel a light stretch on the inside of the straight leg.
exercises.mistake: Don't let the bent knee go far past your toes.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat
exercises.target: Inner thighs, glutes and front of the thighs
exercises.setup: Stand with your feet wide, toes pointing out. Bring your hands together at your chest.
steps: Keeping your body upright, open your knees out and lower down.
Keep your knees over your toes.
Squeeze your inner thighs and glutes as you stand up.
exercises.tip: A wide stance lets you lean forward less than in a normal squat.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your knees cave in.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
steps: Lower into a squat.
Jump up explosively, arms up.
Land softly with your knees slightly bent and go straight into the next squat.
exercises.tip: Try to land without noise; the quieter the landing, the more controlled it is.
exercises.mistake: Don't land with locked knees; if your knee hurts, do a normal squat.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Forward Bend
exercises.setup: Stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent.
steps: As you lean your body forward, extend the other leg backwards; body and leg form one line.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstring.
Squeeze your glutes to return upright; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: If your balance is shaky, support yourself with one hand on a wall.
exercises.mistake: Don't round your back; don't let your hip open to the side.

exercises.name: Pulse Squat
exercises.setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, lower into a squat position.
steps: Stay down.
Rise a few centimetres and lower again; do small pulses.
Keep going for the whole time without standing all the way up.
exercises.tip: A burning feeling in your legs is normal.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your knees cave in.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Chair Squat
exercises.target: Front of the thighs and glutes (advanced)
exercises.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy chair. Stand on one leg and extend the other leg forward.
steps: Sit down slowly onto the chair on one leg; reach your arms forward.
Stop when your hips touch the chair.
Stand up on the same leg; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: The road to the single-leg squat; if it's too hard, use one leg on the way down and two on the way up.
exercises.mistake: Don't drop onto the chair; take 3 seconds to lower.
